findings.source_passage: leaves the highest honors that this air can give, to those men who become famous more through their infinite inferiority to the choice hidden handful of the Divine Inert, than through their undoubted superiority over the dead level of the mass
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'That certain sultanism of his brain'
findings.why_it_matters: The 'Divine Inert' and 'dead level of the mass' formulation is one of the most philosophically distinctive and critically engaged passages in the chapter, essential to understanding Melville's political-metaphysical argument about power and genius; it is entirely missing from the draft.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore verbatim or near-verbatim: 'and leaves the highest honors that this air can give, to those men who become famous more through their infinite inferiority to the choice hidden handful of the Divine Inert, than through their undoubted superiority over the dead level of the mass.'

findings.source_passage: all outward majestical trappings and housings are denied me. Oh, Ahab! what shall be grand in thee, it must needs be plucked at from the skies
findings.why_it_matters: The phrase 'all outward majestical trappings and housings are denied me' is a critical self-positioning statement by the narrator about his relationship to epic convention; erasing it removes interpretive weight about the novel's claim to tragic grandeur through non-aristocratic means.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore: 'and therefore all outward majestical trappings and housings are denied me' before the 'Oh, Ahab!' apostrophe.

findings.source_passage: in this episode touching Emperors and Kings, I must not conceal that I have only to do with a poor old whale-hunter like him
findings.why_it_matters: The self-conscious parenthetical 'I must not conceal' is a signature gesture of the narrator's ironic self-awareness and meta-narrative voice; stripping it to bare fact removes the narrator's characteristic intrusion.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore Ishmael's self-conscious framing: 'in this episode touching Emperors and Kings, I must not conceal that I have only to do with a poor old whale-hunter like him.'

findings.source_passage: never mind how much like an old Mesopotamian family these whalemen may, in some primitive instances, live together
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'Though the long period of a Southern whaling voyage'
findings.why_it_matters: The 'old Mesopotamian family' image is a rhetorically and culturally distinctive Melvillean aside that establishes the narrator's characteristic reach into antiquity; the draft replaces it with the colorless 'family-likeness,' erasing the voice entirely.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'like an old Mesopotamian family' in the clause about whalemen living together.

findings.source_passage: Such large virtue lurks in these small things when extreme political superstitions invest them, that in some royal instances even to idiot imbecility they have imparted potency
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'That certain sultanism of his brain'
findings.why_it_matters: The draft reduces this to 'thus baubles magnify even idiot imbecility,' stripping Melville's precise rhetorical formulation ('large virtue lurks in these small things,' 'extreme political superstitions invest them') which is philosophically and stylistically distinctive.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore: 'Such large virtue lurks in these small things when extreme political superstitions invest them, that in some royal instances even to idiot imbecility they have imparted potency.'

findings.source_passage: But Ahab, my Captain, still moves before me in all his Nantucket grimness and shagginess
findings.why_it_matters: 'Shagginess' alongside 'grimness' is a characteristic double-adjective that contributes to the physical texture of Ahab's presence; its omission slightly deflates the image.

summary: The draft commits two high-severity losses—the 'Divine Inert / dead level of the mass' philosophical passage and the 'outward majestical trappings and housings are denied me' narrator self-positioning—plus multiple medium-severity voice flattenings that collectively erase the chapter's most philosophically and rhetorically distinctive material.
